title: Your Electronics Just Got Closer to Home: India's Chip Manufacturing Push
description: India is actively building factories to produce **semiconductor chips**, the tiny "brains" of all electronics. This effort, backed by significant government i.

faq.q: What is the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)?
faq.a: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) is a government initiative launched in December 2021 to build a robust semiconductor and display manufacturing ecosystem in India by providing financial incentives and support to companies.

faq.q: How much money is the government investing?
faq.a: Under the Semicon India Programme, the government has approved a significant financial outlay, with incentives covering up to 50% of the project cost for eligible semiconductor and display manufacturing projects. The total approved investment across 12 projects under ISM 1.0 is around ₹1.64 lakh crore (approximately US$18 billion in 2026).

faq.q: Which companies are involved in India's chip manufacturing?
faq.a: Several global and Indian companies are involved. Key players include Micron Technology, which has an operational OSAT facility in Gujarat, and Tata Electronics, which has an OSAT facility under pilot production in Assam and is developing a large fab in Gujarat in partnership with PSMC.

faq.q: How long will it take for India to make its own chips?
faq.a: Setting up a semiconductor fab is a multi-year process. While OSAT facilities like Micron's and Tata's have begun commercial and pilot production, the larger silicon fabrication plants (fabs) are expected to start production between 2027 and 2029.

faq.q: Will this make my current phone cheaper right away?
faq.a: Not immediately. The impact on consumer prices will likely be gradual as domestic production scales up and becomes a significant part of the supply chain. It's a long-term strategy for cost reduction and supply security.
